CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Bulukumba Regency.
2. Government is a body or organization that exercises the governmental power of a state. The Government has the duty to administer governmental affairs, from the central level, province, regency, municipality, sub-district, village, to hamlet.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Regional Apparatus is an organization/Institution in the regional government that is responsible to the Regent in the context of administering government consisting of regional secretary, regional agencies and regional technical institutions, sub-districts, villages and civil service police units according to regional needs.
5. Agency is a Regional Apparatus that has the main duties and functions in carrying out Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Bulukumba Regency.
6. Village Government is the administration of governmental affairs and the interests of the local community in the governmental system of the unitary state of the Republic of Indonesia.
7. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the annual financial plan of the regional government that is discussed and approved jointly by the Regional Government and DPRD, and stipulated by Regional Regulation.
8. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter referred to as APBDes is the annual financial plan of the village government that is discussed and approved jointly by the Village Head and Village Representative Body which is stipulated through Village Regulation.
9. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
10. Implementation of Women and Child Protection is a directed, integrated, and sustainable effort carried out by the Central Government, Regional Government, Village Government, and community to fulfill the rights of women and children as citizens within the scope of this Regional Regulation.
11. Women's Protection is all efforts to protect and provide a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
12. Women and Child Protection is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, and or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty.
16. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, and arbitrary deprivation of liberty whether occurring in the private or public sphere.
17. Victim is a person who experiences physical suffering, women and children who experience violence and/or mental threats and or economic loss resulting from an act of violence.
18. Victim of Violence is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from criminal acts of violence.
19. Violence Prevention is any action or effort undertaken to eliminate various factors that cause acts of violence against women and children.
20. Community is individual Indonesian citizens, community groups, and/or Mass Organizations.
21. Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPT PPA is an operational technical implementation unit in a work unit that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an integrated service provider for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems.
22. Child-Friendly Regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
23. Assistance for Victims of Violence is an effort or process to assist victims of violence in accessing the right to handling, protection, and recovery.
24. Rapid Reaction Team hereinafter abbreviated as TRC is a team formed by the agency in charge of Women's Empowerment and Children that is tasked with assisting UPT PPA in conducting outreach and/or assistance to accelerate the process of handling cases of violence against women and children.
25. Women and Child Protection Task Force is a coordinative institution formed by the Bulukumba Regency Government that coordinates policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in Bulukumba Regency.
26. Vulnerable Groups are any person or community group entitled to receive special treatment and protection relating to their specificity. Vulnerable groups as referred to in this regulation consist of women and children in conflict with the law, persons with disabilities, Indonesian migrant workers, the elderly and/or indigenous peoples of ammatoa Kajang.

CHAPTER IV
PREVENTION OF VIOLENCE
Article 5
(1) Prevention of violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a shall be implemented through:
a. planning and implementation of policies, programs, and activities;
b. provision of education; and
c. enhancement of community participation.
(2) Prevention of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be implemented by the Regional Government in an integrated and sustainable manner based on the Regional Long-Term Development Plan and Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.
(3) Planning and implementation of policies, programs and activities as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a namely:
a. integrating the issue of protection of women and children into the policies, programs and activities of Regional Apparatus; and
b. making the issue of protection of women and children one of the priorities of regional development.
(4) Provision of education as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b namely:
a. providing information, guidance and/or counseling;
b. provision of accessibility to obtain education, training, funding, income enhancement and social services;
c. creating a friendly and safe work environment atmosphere for women; and
d. building and providing an information system that is easily accessible;
(5) Enhancement of community participation through involvement of parties as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, namely:
a. building and enhancing community participation and awareness towards prevention and protection of women and children;
b. making regional regulations and encouraging Village Government to make Village Regulations related to protection of women and children; and
c. building networks and cooperation with law enforcement apparatus, private sector/business world, universities, mass media, and non-governmental organizations as well as community institutions that are engaged in and care about women and children.

Article 6
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (3) Letter a Sufficiently clear.
Letter b Sufficiently clear.
Letter c Sufficiently clear.
Letter d Sufficiently clear.
Letter e What is meant by "safe house facilitation" is a place that provides protection, assistance, and services for women and children who are victims of violence or require help. This house functions as a temporary, safe and confidential residence, where victims can receive psychological, legal, and social support for their recovery.
Paragraph (4) Sufficiently clear.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by the principle of humanity is the principle of humanity emphasizes respect and protection of the basic rights of every individual regardless of gender, age, or social status.
This means that women and children have equal rights to live without violence and treatment that degrades human dignity.
Letter b What is meant by the principle of justice and gender equality is this principle emphasizes the need to address gender inequality which is often the root cause of acts of violence against women and children. Protection must ensure that women and children receive fair and equal treatment in the legal system and society without discrimination based on gender.
Letter c What is meant by the principle of protection is proactive and preventive protection against acts of violence. This protection must be carried out through an approach that includes prevention, handling, rehabilitation, and support for victims as well as potential perpetrators so that violence does not occur again.
Letter d What is meant by the principle of best interests for women and children is this principle focuses on the best interests and rights of women and children as the main priority. Protection actions and policies must always prioritize their welfare and interests, including listening to their views and aspirations in the decision-making process.
Letter e What is meant by the principle of non-discrimination is this principle affirms that protection must be carried out without discrimination based on gender, age, ethnic background, religion, or social status. Every individual has equal rights to be protected from acts of violence, without exception.
Letter f What is meant by the principle of special treatment for vulnerable groups is treatment of a group of people who experience vulnerability or physical and non-physical limitations such as women, children, persons with disabilities, pregnant women, the elderly, minority groups, people with mental disorders and poor people.

"Perdagangan" in this context is trafficking (human trafficking/trafficking in persons). Since the retrieved English passage accurately reflects this and the judge correctly relied on it, the golden label of "No" appears incorrect; the policy does address trafficking (at least for children).

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration with the principle of autonomy as broad as possible, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has mandated to provide protection for women and children, as well as to provide equal rights for women to participate in contributing to various aspects of development. This is also reaffirmed in Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government regarding the division of governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection. In line with this, Regional Governments which have the principles of autonomy and co-administration with the principle of autonomy as broad as possible, also strive to realize the ideals contained in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.

Based on this, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has the desire to realize its commitment in order to provide protection for women and children so that their rights can be fulfilled as well as to realize gender equality and justice in all aspects in accordance with human dignity, and to optimize women's empowerment, child protection, and gender mainstreaming in the region so that efforts need to be made involving all parties in various aspects of development.

In an effort to realize this commitment, the Regional Government of Bulukumba Regency has established a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children which regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively while also serving as proof of the seriousness of the commitment of the Bulukumba Regency Government in protecting the rights of women and children as well as providing a legal umbrella in fighting for their rights.

Article 19
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector as referred to in Article 15 letter c shall be implemented in the form of private sector participation. (2) The role of the private sector as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of: a. providing protection for women and children through corporate social and environmental responsibility programs;
b. providing support to the government, community institutions, civil society organizations and the community in the context of protection of women and children; and
c. actively participating in business organizations that have a commitment to the protection of women and children.

REGENT OF BULUKUMBA
PROVINCE OF SOUTH SULAWESI
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BULUKUMBA REGENCY NUMBER 3 OF 2024
CONCERNING
THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
BY THE GRACE OF THE ALMIGHTY GOD

6.7.rationale: The original Indonesian text mentions minority/isolated groups explicitly only for children (Pasal 16 ayat (3) huruf c: "anak dari kelompok minoritas dan terisolasi"). For women, the regulation does not explicitly identify women from minority/isolated groups as a specific target group, nor does it set special measures for them. While the elucidation of nondiscrimination mentions protection without discrimination based on "latar belakang etnis" etc., that is a general principle rather than targeted intersectional measures for minority women. Thus the judge’s "No" is consistent with the policy text, and the golden label "Yes" likely is wrong.
